M4.2.title: M2 - Semantica, geometria e invariantes
M4.2.supported_claim: Long/short barrier geometry, exact horizon and mandatory normalization by an approved horizon log-volatility scale.
M4.2.does_not_support: A volatility estimator or probability model.

M4.2.title: M3 - Contratos de datos pre-trade
M4.2.supported_claim: Plan identity, closed Binance USD-M klines, timestamps, freshness and missing-data behavior.

M4.2.title: Binance USD-M Futures Kline/Candlestick Data
M4.2.supported_claim: Kline fields, intervals, timestamps and units.

M4.2.title: Modeling and Forecasting Realized Volatility
M4.2.supported_claim: Realized volatility constructed from high-frequency returns is linked to quadratic variation and can be modeled over time.
M4.2.does_not_support: Using one lagged horizon as an exact forecast for crypto, a universal sampling interval, or a TP/SL probability.

M4.2.title: Boundary Crossing Probability for Brownian Motion
M4.2.supported_claim: Boundary crossing is a path-dependent first-passage problem that requires a specified stochastic process and boundary.
M4.2.does_not_support: Brownian motion as an accepted crypto model or any project probability before M6.

M4.2.title: Forecast Bitcoin Volatility with Least Squares Model Averaging
M4.2.supported_claim: Bitcoin realized-volatility forecasting is an empirical model selection problem with competing specifications.
M4.2.does_not_support: Transfer to all six pairs, barrier probabilities, or a fixed project estimator without independent validation.

M4.3.supported_claim: Closed OHLC timestamps, plan and missing-data policy.
Exact horizon sampling, log returns and previous-horizon RV.
Recursive exponential smoothing and dependence on alpha and initialization.
M4.3.does_not_support: EMA periods 9/21/50/200, crossover signals or crypto returns.

M4.3.supported_claim: Time-series parameters may change through latent regimes that must be estimated by a specified model.
M4.3.does_not_support: Calling arbitrary indicator bands regimes or assigning direction.

M4.3.supported_claim: Realized-volatility components across heterogeneous horizons may contain distinct temporal information.
M4.3.does_not_support: The project H/2H/4H price-direction hierarchy or fixed weights.

M4.3.supported_claim: Time-series momentum was documented for 58 traditional futures at monthly horizons.
M4.3.does_not_support: Crypto intraday transfer, TP-first probabilities or EMA stacks.

M4.3.supported_claim: Technical-rule results in cryptocurrencies vary by asset and out-of-sample period; Bitcoin lacked OOS predictability in their test.
M4.3.does_not_support: Any selected project rule, period, threshold or pair-wide transfer.

M4.3.supported_claim: Published FX support/resistance levels predicted some intraday trend interruptions, with performance varying by pair and firm.
M4.3.does_not_support: Rolling extrema as equivalent levels, crypto transfer or a penalty.

M4.3.supported_claim: Local extrema and prior bounces can be studied as price-memory candidates, with time scale and bounce count as parameters.
M4.3.does_not_support: A universal extrema detector or project TP/SL probability.

M4.4.supported_claim: Fields, timestamps, retention and absence policy for Binance Futures and Spot observations.
M4.4.does_not_support: Any predictive sign, threshold, weight or score.

M4.4.supported_claim: Exact horizon, closed-window and log-geometry conventions.
Price displacement and non-additive interaction conventions.
Official meanings and availability of aggregate trades, taker volume, open interest, mark/index prices and funding fields.
M4.4.does_not_support: Predictiveness, full-book order flow, complete retention or universal funding interpretation.

M4.4.supported_claim: Official Spot best bid and ask fields.
M4.4.does_not_support: Provider event time for REST bookTicker or basis predictiveness.

M4.4.supported_claim: Short-interval price changes in the studied equities were more robustly related to full order-book event imbalance than to trade volume or trade imbalance alone.
M4.4.does_not_support: Calling Binance taker-trade imbalance OFI, crypto transfer, project horizons or a TP/SL probability.

M4.4.supported_claim: Open-interest changes contained information in the traditional futures markets and horizons studied by the authors.
M4.4.does_not_support: Crypto perpetual intraday transfer, long/short direction from gross OI, quadrant labels or project weights.

M4.4.supported_claim: Their Bitcoin sample found spot leading the restricted exchange-traded futures market in price discovery.
M4.4.does_not_support: Binance perpetual leadership, basis direction or all crypto pairs and horizons.

M4.4.supported_claim: A later Bitcoin study found futures generally leading spot with daily variation after accounting for noise.
M4.4.does_not_support: A fixed leader, Binance perpetual transfer or a basis signal.

M4.4.supported_claim: Funding is an anchoring cash-flow mechanism for perpetuals and spot-perpetual deviations can remain material.
M4.4.does_not_support: Funding sign as a standalone return forecast, Binance-specific thresholds or ignoring trading costs.

M4.5.supported_claim: Pre-trade outcome space, TP/SL geometry, pending-entry branches and immutable analysis identity.
M4.5.does_not_support: Probabilities, trading costs or decision policy.

M4.5.supported_claim: Available bid/ask, depth, mark/funding, exchange filters, user-plan margin/leverage and authenticated commission fields.
M4.5.does_not_support: Future exit liquidity, future funding, account liquidation price or predictive effects.

M4.5.supported_claim: Observed funding state and the prohibition on treating the last funding rate as a future rate.
Official availability and field meanings for order-book, best-quote, mark-price and funding observations.
M4.5.does_not_support: Guaranteed fills, future order-book state, slippage thresholds or TP/SL probability.

M4.5.supported_claim: Authenticated maker, taker and RPI commission-rate fields.
M4.5.does_not_support: A universal rate, the liquidity role of an unknown future fill or future exit notional.

M4.5.supported_claim: Implementation shortfall compares signed execution VWAP with the arrival midpoint; fill rate and unfilled quantity matter.
M4.5.does_not_support: Crypto-specific impact coefficients, future exit slippage or a fixed minimum slippage.

M4.5.supported_claim: Execution has transaction-cost, market-impact and timing-risk components.
M4.5.does_not_support: The exact project book-sweep estimator, universal parameters or directional market probability.

M4.5.supported_claim: Positive perpetual funding transfers value from long positions to short positions and anchors perpetual prices.
M4.5.does_not_support: Future Binance funding rates, a standalone return forecast or project probability weights.

M4.5.supported_claim: Leverage magnifies gains and losses relative to invested capital.
M4.5.does_not_support: Binance perpetual liquidation mechanics, maintenance-margin brackets or a safe leverage threshold.
